correctness.rationale: Wrapping preserves integer Fourier moments; the exponential and Erlang moments at r are θ/(θ−ir) and its square. With A=1+θ² one obtains u=θ²/A−2qθ²/A² and v=θ/A+qθ(θ²−1)/A². Substitution gives D=|m−1/2|²−1/4=q²θ²/A² and v+√D=θ(1−u). Since q≥0 and u<1, the positive branch gives the claimed inverse; the (θ,q) Jacobian is 2qθ²/A³ and vanishes at the null. Under the null the gradient g=(2u−1,2v) has norm 1 and g·(u,v)=u. The second raw moment of g·(cos T,sin T) is (1+Re[(g₁−ig₂)² θ/(θ−2i)])/2. Subtracting u² gives the stated positive V(θ). The bounded vector triangular-array CLT and quadratic Taylor remainder give centered variance V(θ₀) for θ_n→θ₀>0 and q_n→0; the plug-in converges to θ₀ and the scaled population D at q_n=c n^(−1/4) gives exactly the claimed mean shift. At fixed q>0 the population D is positive and v/(1−u)>0, so the test is consistent. For the lower bound, differentiation of the unwrapped exponential then wrapping gives k_θ−h_θ=−θ∂_θh_θ. With θ in a compact positive-rate neighborhood, Taylor error against h_{θ(1−q)} is uniformly O(q²), and its density floor is strictly positive. The squared Hellinger distance is O(q⁴), tensorizes at most linearly in n and implies TV→0 below the fourth-root scale. The nearby null sequence stays in the neighborhood, so uniform near-rate size control, not merely pointwise size, suffices for the impossibility bound. No all-rate uniform calibration or local-efficiency claim is established. The supplied checker.py was read, not executed; it tests moments, inversion and variance on finite grids, not the limiting-testing theorem.

value.rationale: A fitting model already in use has a singular null when its rate is unknown. The result turns that singularity into a usable first-moment test with explicit local power and a matching impossibility scale for any test with local uniform size control. These are concrete inferential consequences beyond deriving another moment formula, without asserting optimal power, finite-sample size control or robustness to an unknown angular origin.
